name: using-superpowers
description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, ignore this skill.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Platform Adaptation

If your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions:

- Claude Code: `references/claude-code-tools.md`
- Codex: `references/codex-tools.md`
- Pi: `references/pi-tools.md`
- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`
- Hermes Agent: `references/hermes-tools.md`
- Muse: `references/muse-tools.md`

## User Instructions

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.

name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT

  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   topic procedures. Enter the procedure before its supporting reference. Do not
   load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting action buttons, including their labels, roles, emphasis, hit regions, and platform behavior.

# Operate on buttons

Read [the buttons guide](../../references/buttons.md) before making HIG claims. This procedure is application advice for turning that guide into an artifact; platform facts and dimensions come from the guide. Preserve the user's framework and authorized scope.

## Establish the action contract

Inspect the supplied screen, code, prototype, or brief. Identify the target platform, input methods, surrounding task, and requested mode: create, review, or adapt. For each consequential button, record its visible label or symbol, activation outcome, affected object, reversibility, current role/default status, and actual hit region if available. A screenshot can establish visible styling; it cannot establish hit geometry, keyboard behavior, or accessible names. Mark those as unknown and inspect implementation when available.

Classify the action before styling it. An immediate command fits a button. A persistent on/off setting may need a toggle; choosing one of several persistent options may need a segmented control or picker; a menu-opening control needs the corresponding menu button behavior. Retain a button when its action is to open that choice, but distinguish opening from committing a choice.

## Make and apply the consequential choices

1. Write an outcome-specific short verb phrase, or use a familiar symbol whose meaning survives its context. Give an icon-only control an accessible name that states the action. Do not assume a tooltip replaces the name. On Mac, an ellipsis indicates that another window, view, or app requires further input; add it based on the continuation, not merely because an operation takes time.
2. Assign semantic roles from consequences. Prefer one or two prominent likely actions per view and use style rather than unequal sizes to rank related choices. A primary/default action should normally be the likely nondestructive choice. If destruction is involved, consult the alerts topic before deciding confirmation and Return behavior: the guide explicitly allows a deliberate-destruction alert exception, so “destructive can never be default” is not a universal rule. Cancel abandons the current task; it is not a generic label for completing it.
3. Choose the system control/style when available, retaining its states and accessibility behavior. For a custom control, specify perceivable press feedback and preserve meaningful focus, enabled/disabled, and selected states as applicable. State the reason for a disabled action when the surrounding context does not explain it. This is application advice, not a new Apple requirement to add all states to every button.
4. Check visual and selectable geometry separately. Apply the guide's target and separation rules for the actual platform; a small glyph or small visual style does not establish a small hit region. On visionOS, retain a discernible shape/fill, use standard audible/state feedback, and inspect center spacing and hover overlap. Do not propose unsupported custom hover effects or haptics there. On watchOS, choose inline versus toolbar placement deliberately; preserve common heights for peer controls and use short labels for side-by-side actions. On Mac, distinguish view-body square/image/help buttons from toolbar items; apply the help-button placement/count rules only when designing Help.
5. Only when the command has delayed completion, define the initiating, waiting, and resolved behavior. On iOS/iPadOS, use the activating button's activity indication as described in the guide, preserving context and replacing its image when appropriate. Specify how duplicate activation is handled and what success or failure means in the product; do not promise network completion from a press animation.

Perform the authorized work: implement the controls in the supplied project for a build request; produce an annotated control specification for a design request; or report evidence-backed defects and exact corrections for a review. For adaptation, map each affected control to its destination platform rather than copying appearance alone.

## Deliver and verify

Return the changed artifact or a compact button contract containing label/name, outcome, role/default, style/placement, target region, and relevant state behavior. In review mode attach findings to identifiable controls and separate observed defects from checks requiring execution.

Verify that activation reaches the named outcome; cancellation leaves the intended prior state; keyboard/default activation cannot commit an unintended outcome; focus and accessible names identify the action; and enlarged labels do not clip or overlap adjacent targets. Measure hit regions from layout/runtime data when available. Fail the design if a destructive consequence is mislabeled, peer targets overlap, an icon has no discoverable name, or custom press feedback is absent. State separately which checks were inspected in source, exercised, or remain Apple-device checks; Linux inspection does not prove gaze, VoiceOver, haptics, or native rendering.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** A Mac photo organizer has equally prominent `Go`, `Remove`, and `Close` buttons. `Go` opens export settings; `Remove` deletes a selection with undo; `Close` finishes editing metadata.

**Decision:** The labels hide three different contracts. Export requires further input; routine reversible removal does not by itself justify a confirmation alert; finishing edits should name completion. The export task, rather than removal, is the likely action on this screen.

**After:** Specify `Export…` as the prominent action opening export settings, `Remove Photos` as a lower-emphasis command with a visible Undo path, and `Done` for finishing metadata edits. Inspect actual save semantics before changing `Close` to `Done`. Verify the Return mapping, undo restoration, and that each accessible name matches the resulting action. These product choices are an example application, not facts about the unseen implementation.

## Conditional handoffs

Load alerts for consequential confirmation/default decisions; toggles or segmented-controls for persistent selection; pop-up-buttons or pull-down-buttons for menu-opening behavior; toolbars when placement belongs to window chrome; and accessibility when naming, focus, contrast, or target access needs deeper work. Keep this button contract as the input to the next topic.

name: apple-hig-accessibility
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting Apple-platform interfaces for text enlargement, sensory access, assistive input, motor access, cognitive needs, or accessibility preferences.

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Buttons Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. ## Contents - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Style](#Style) - [Content](#Content) - [Role](#Role) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) A button performs an immediate action. Its visual style, visible symbol/text, and semantic role work together to explain what activation does. ## Best practices Allow enough surrounding space for clear separation and easy selection. General hit regions should be at least 44×44 pt; visionOS targets need 60×60 pt. Custom buttons always need press feedback. ## Style Prefer system styles for built-in states, accessibility, and appearance adaptation. Use one or two prominent buttons per view for likely actions. Distinguish a preferred option through style rather than making related buttons different sizes. Keep label colors distinct from colorful content; the default monochrome often works best over rich backgrounds. ## Content Use a familiar symbol for a familiar action; use a short title-case verb phrase when words are clearer. Mac and visionOS can provide brief hover tooltips; text-labeled buttons usually explain themselves. ## Role Normal has no special meaning; primary is the expected/default action; Cancel abandons the current action; destructive signals data loss. Roles affect rendering, such as accent fill for primary and red for destructive. Primary can respond to Return and close a temporary view. Generally assign primary only to a nondestructive likely action. Application advice: consult the alert-specific deliberate-destruction exception before prescribing confirmation behavior. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS For delayed completion, show an activity indicator within the activating button, optionally changing its label to the current operation. The indicator replaces any button image while preserving context for the wait. ### macOS #### Push buttons The standard push button can show text, imagery, or both and can serve as default. Use flexible height for tall icons or multiple text lines, otherwise retain standard sizing. Append an ellipsis when the button opens another window/view/app for further input. Consider spring loading through a dragged selection plus force-click on Magic Trackpad, preserving the drag afterward. #### Square buttons These small glyph-only controls affect a nearby view, for example adding/removing table rows. They can act as push, toggle, or pop-up controls. Use them in the body rather than the frame, toolbar, or status bar. Prefer system symbols and omit introductory labels when proximity explains the function. #### Help buttons Use the familiar system question-mark control, at most one per window, opening context-specific help when possible and top-level help otherwise. In a dialog with dismissal controls, place it in the opposite lower corner, aligned vertically with those controls. Without dismissal controls, or in settings, use either lower corner. Keep it in the view body and omit explanatory introductory text. #### Image buttons Image buttons can act as push, toggle, or pop-up controls inside a view. Toolbar imagery instead belongs to a toolbar item. Allow about 10 pixels between image and clickable button edges and generally omit a visible system border. Put any needed label beneath the image. ### visionOS Buttons normally have a visible background and audible feedback. Circle suits glyph-only content, rounded rectangle or capsule suits text, and capsule suits text plus glyph. Standard states supply feedback; custom hover effects are not supported. A look-triggered tooltip can explain a glyph. | Shape | Supported visual sizes | | --- | --- | | Circle | Mini 28 pt; small 32 pt; regular 44 pt; large 52 pt; extra large 64 pt | | Text capsule | Small 32 pt; regular 44 pt; large 52 pt | | Text-and-icon capsule | Regular 44 pt; large 52 pt | | Rounded rectangle | Small 32 pt; regular 44 pt; large 52 pt | Visual size does not remove the 60-pt targeting requirement. Use a discernible shape/fill except inside a larger clearly bounded toolbar, menu, alert, or ornament. On window glass, thin material suits the button; floating in space, use glass. Reserve white fill with black content for the system's toggled state. Prefer round/capsule forms for steady gaze, and a capsule for a standalone button. Keep centers at least 60 pt apart; add 4 pt padding around buttons 60 pt or larger to prevent hover overlap. Avoid rows/stacks of mini/small buttons. Prefer rounded rectangles for vertical text stacks and capsules for horizontal rows. Standard sounds matter because visionOS provides no haptics. ### watchOS Inline buttons are capsules with a contrasting material. Put corner actions in a toolbar so the system relocates title/time and gives controls Liquid Glass. Full-width buttons suit primary actions. Side-by-side buttons should share height and use short labels or glyphs; vertical one- and two-line buttons should also maintain common heights. Toolbar actions can navigate related areas or operate on current content. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Pop-up buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pop-up-buttons) [Pull-down buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pull-down-buttons) [Toggles](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/toggles) [Segmented controls](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/segmented-controls) [Location button](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Location-button) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: December 16, 2025, June 9, 2025, February 2, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023, June 5, 2023. # Accessibility Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. The source requires two confirmations for actions that are difficult to reverse, such as deletion, in this mode. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or watchOS beyond the guidance above. ### visionOS Support hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. Do not lock content to the head, which can feel confining and interfere with Pointer Control. Minimize large or repeated gestures and consider the physical surroundings. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, June 10, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.

Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Progress UI is temporary feedback during work, disappearing when it finishes. Determinate indicators represent measurable completion with a leading-to-trailing bar or clockwise circular fill. Indeterminate indicators communicate ongoing activity without a completion estimate; every platform has a spinner, and macOS also has an indeterminate bar. ## Best practices Prefer measurable progress when possible and report it honestly. Estimate the whole operation so an early sprint to 90% does not conceal a much longer final stage. Keep activity visibly ongoing, and explain stalls with a useful recovery route. When duration becomes known, an indeterminate bar can become determinate; avoid changing a spinner into a differently shaped bar midtask because that disrupts layout and interpretation. Add a short, specific task description only when it supplies real context. Choose a consistent place for status. Allow cancellation where it is safe; offer pause as well when cancel would discard useful partial work. Explain consequential cancellation and let the person either confirm it or resume. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS or visionOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS #### Refresh content controls Pull-to-refresh reveals an activity indicator when people drag down a content view. It supplements periodic automatic refreshes rather than making users responsible for every update. An optional title should convey useful content context, such as the previous update time, rather than explaining the pull gesture or merely restating that loading is occurring. ### macOS Both animated bars and spinners can represent indeterminate work. Prefer a small spinner for asynchronous background operations or tight spaces, such as beside a control or within a field. Usually omit spinner labels when the initiating action already explains the activity. ### watchOS Progress bars, circular fills, and spinners default to white against the scene background. Tint can customize their color. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — UIKit — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: September 12, 2023, June 5, 2023. # Alerts Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. An alert interrupts to communicate urgent, critical information and useful actions, including problems, unexpected data loss, or important confirmations. ## Best practices Reserve alerts for situations that warrant immediate attention. Put informational status in context when no action is required. Common undoable deletions generally need no confirmation; uncommon irreversible destruction does. Avoid startup alerts: cached or placeholder content with a discreet problem explanation is often a better response to an unavailable network. ## Anatomy Alerts are modal and adapt their appearance to iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS rather than using one universal layout. ## Content Use a title, optional message, and up to three buttons. iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS can include text fields; macOS and visionOS can include an icon and accessory view. macOS additionally supports a suppression checkbox and Help button. Use direct, neutral, approachable wording without blaming the person or concealing severity. The title should explain what happened, its context, and cause as concisely as possible, generally within two lines. Avoid a bare error label or code. Complete-sentence titles use sentence case and punctuation; fragments use title case without punctuation. Additional text should add information in brief complete sentences. Clear action labels should make button explanations unnecessary; if instructions are unavoidable, use device-neutral language such as choose and the exact title without quotation marks. Include an input field only when resolving the situation requires it, with secure entry for passwords. ## Buttons Use short, usually one- or two-word, title-case action labels without punctuation. Prefer specific outcomes over Yes/No or ambiguous OK; reserve OK for purely informational acknowledgment. A cancellation action is always Cancel. Place the expected/default action at the trailing end of a row or top of a stack, with cancellation generally leading or at the bottom. Apply destructive styling to destructive consequences the person did not deliberately request. A confirmation of an explicitly chosen destruction, such as Empty Trash, can retain a normal default action so Return confirms intent. Always provide Cancel alongside destructive actions, but do not make Cancel the default. To force a deliberate reading, consider no default. A single default acknowledgment button should be Done rather than Cancel. Support familiar alternate cancellation where appropriate: Home Screen exit on iOS/iPadOS; Escape or Command-Period on attached keyboards in iOS/iPadOS/macOS/visionOS; Menu on the tvOS remote. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS or watchOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS Use action sheets for multiple choices following an intentional action. Keep titles and optional messages short to minimize scrolling, while accommodating enlarged accessibility text. ### macOS The app icon appears automatically but can be replaced. Repeating alerts can offer suppression; necessary details can use an accessory view, and Help can open documentation. Reserve a caution symbol for situations needing extra attention, particularly unexpected loss, rather than routine overwrite, save, or empty-trash tasks. ### visionOS In Shared Space, an alert sits slightly in front of its parent window and stays attached when the window moves. In Full Space, it centers in the wearer's field of view. An accessory view must be no taller than 154 pt and use a 16-pt corner radius. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Modality](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/modality) [Action sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/action-sheets) [Sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: February 2, 2024, September 12, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# iPad field-report export controls: correction plan

## Scope and evidence

This is a specification review of "'`interface.md`, not an inspection of a running app. Its statements are the evidence for current behavior: four equally prominent filled buttons; Delete is primary/default; Preview is glyph-only with no accessible name; actual hit regions are 20 × 20 pt with 2 pt gaps; Publish takes eight seconds without feedback and repeat activation creates duplicate uploads. All four functions must remain available. No framework or Apple SDK is assumed.

## Ranked verified findings

Ranking is a product-risk judgment, not an Apple severity scale. “Verified” below means explicitly established by the supplied brief.

| Rank | Finding and effect | Correction and source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — High | Publish gives no feedback for eight seconds and repeat taps create duplicate uploads. People cannot tell whether publishing started and can publish repeatedly. | Immediately show activity inside Publish, label it “Publishing…”, and atomically guard all activation paths. Add request deduplication and explicit completion/failure states. The activity treatment follows [Buttons — iOS, iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons#iOS-iPadOS); deduplication is engineering advice to meet this product'"'s outcome. |
| 2 — High | Delete is the editor's primary/default action. Accidental default activation can select data loss. Actual deletion scope and reversibility are unknown. | Make Publish the likely primary command; remove Delete's default mapping and prominent fill. Give Delete destructive semantics and a separate position. Generally primary should be a likely nondestructive action: [Buttons — Role](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons#Role). Resolve recovery as specified below before implementation. |
| 3 — High | Every actual target is 20 × 20 pt, with only 2 pt gaps. This increases selection difficulty and risk of choosing a neighbor, especially Delete. | Use at least 44 × 44 pt activation regions, sufficient width for labels, and clear separation. Proposed layout uses 12 pt between target boundaries and 24 pt before Delete. These gaps are product choices, not a universal HIG spacing requirement. [Buttons — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons#Best-practices) recommends at least 44 × 44 pt general targets. |
| 4 — High | Glyph-only Preview has no accessible name, so its action is not identified to assistive input. | Show “Preview” and expose button role/name “Preview”. A retained decorative glyph must not create a second spoken label. [Accessibility — Vision and Mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Mobility) supports meaningful descriptions and labeled controls. |
| 5 — Medium | Four equally prominent filled buttons conceal priority and give destructive Delete the same visual emphasis as routine actions. | Keep one filled primary, Publish. Use lower-emphasis Preview and Save Draft, and a spatially separate destructive Delete. Keep peer target heights consistent; use style rather than unequal sizes for hierarchy. [Buttons — Style](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons#Style) advises one or two prominent likely actions per view. |

The local guides differ in their numerical framing: Buttons gives general targets of at least 44 × 44 pt; Accessibility lists iPadOS 44 × 44 pt default and 28 × 28 pt minimum. This plan conservatively chooses 44 × 44 pt or larger. The supplied 20 × 20 pt fails both. The smaller accessibility minimum is not a reason to retain dense controls.

## Decisions and corrected action contract

All four are commands, so buttons remain appropriate; none represents persistent selection. The footer is retained. Proposed order: a separate leading Delete, then Save Draft, Preview, and trailing Publish. At narrow editor widths or enlarged text, wrap into stable rows with full labels and nonoverlapping targets; never shrink targets to fit. All custom buttons need visible press feedback, focus indication, and exposed enabled/busy states. Do not rely on red alone to identify Delete.

| Control | Outcome and scope | Role, availability and recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Publish | Publish a captured revision of the current report, including its attachments. This scope is a proposed contract, to validate against the service. | Sole primary, filled; enabled when publishable and no unresolved publish operation exists. It never deletes or dismisses unfinished work. Focused activation works; any editor-level default mapping must be Publish, never Delete, and must not intercept Return in text editing. |
| Preview | Open a read-only preview of the current report revision. | Normal, lower emphasis; visible and accessible label “Preview”. Closing returns to the editor and initiating control without losing edits. Remains usable during upload. |
| Save Draft | Persist the current editable report without publishing. | Normal, lower emphasis. Report actual save success/failure and preserve unsaved edits on failure. Remains usable during upload if draft persistence is independent; serialize it safely if the existing service shares mutable state. Never silently discard it. |
| Delete | Remove the current report, with exact local/remote scope disclosed before committing. | Destructive, lower emphasis, never the editor default. Block while Publish is unresolved, with nearby explanation “Available after publishing finishes.” |

Deletion recovery is not established by the brief. Conservative proposed behavior until its scope is resolved: activating Delete opens a confirmation identifying the report and exact loss, with Delete and Cancel and no default action. Cancel and supported keyboard cancellation leave the report intact and restore focus. Do not claim that confirmation already exists or is universally required. If investigation establishes routine, fully undoable deletion, prefer immediate deletion with a reliable Undo path instead of routine confirmation. If Assistive Access is supported, separately implement its documented two-confirmation treatment for difficult-to-reverse actions. [Alerts — Best practices and Buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts#Buttons) permits a default confirmation for deliberately requested destruction; the editor's unsafe default does not justify a blanket ban on that exception.

## Slow-upload state model

The eight seconds are observed duration in the brief, not a timer for declaring success. Show an indeterminate activity indicator **inside the activating Publish button**, replacing any image while retaining its label context and stable geometry. Use “Publishing…” and expose busy/unavailable semantics with a concise status announcement. Do not move focus or announce every animation frame. A spinner alone must not be the only accessible state.

Use measured progress only if the service can describe meaningful whole-operation completion; never invent percentages from elapsed time. If bytes reach 100% before server commit, say “Finishing publication…” rather than “Published”. Keep status in a stable location. Persistent success/error text should remain readable without a forced short timeout. [Progress indicators — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators#Best-practices) supports honest progress, stall explanation and safe cancellation.

"'```text
states = idle, publishing, reconciling, failed, published

activatePublish():                     // same handler for touch, keyboard, assistive input
  atomically:
    if state in {publishing, reconciling}: return
    if currentRevision already has acknowledged publication: show existing result; return
    capture immutable reportRevision and attachments
    obtain stable operationKey for this publication intent
    state = publishing                 // guard before starting asynchronous work
  render busy Publish("Publishing…"), status("Publishing report…")
  submit captured revision with operationKey

onAcknowledgedCommit(operationKey, publicationId):
  ignore callbacks for other operations
  record publicationId and captured revision durably
  state = published
  clear activity; show persistent "Published" and result link when available
  if editor has newer edits: show "Published revision; newer changes are unpublished"
  restore Publish only for a new publishable intent/revision

onDefinitiveFailure(operationKey):
  state = failed
  clear activity; show actionable reason and explicit Retry
  retain editor contents and captured operation context
  Retry reuses the key for the same intent

onTransportTimeoutOrLostResponse(operationKey):
  state = reconciling
  show "Publication not yet confirmed. Checking status…"
  query operation status; do not issue a new publication intent
  committed -> onAcknowledgedCommit
  definitively failed -> onDefinitiveFailure
  unknown -> retain guarded state with Check Status recovery
```

Server-side operation keys must return the same publication result for duplicate requests; a UI guard alone cannot cover retries or lost responses. Persist pending operation identity if navigation/reload can occur. These are proposed engineering requirements, not claims that the existing backend supports them. If no deduplication/status service exists, build that capability or expose an unresolved state that prevents unsafe retries; do not label uncertain publication as failed and start a fresh upload.

Keep editing, Preview and independent Save Draft usable; publish the captured revision rather than racing with later edits. Do not offer Cancel Upload until the service can guarantee what cancellation means. If safe cancellation is implemented, distinguish “request cancellation” from confirmed cancellation, preserve the draft, and resolve any concurrent server commit. No modal alert is needed for routine waiting.

## Worked before/after

**Before:** A field worker taps Publish at t=0. Nothing changes. At t=2 they tap again. The supplied behavior creates another upload. At approximately t=8 there is still no specified completion feedback. Delete remains equally prominent and the default.

**After (proposed):** At t=0 the first activation synchronously enters publishing and captures revision R17. Publish contains an activity indicator and reads “Publishing…”. At t=2 touch or keyboard reactivation creates no additional operation. Preview still opens R17/current content according to its clearly identified revision; later edits can be saved as R18. At t=8, **if** the server acknowledges R17, activity ends and the editor says “Published revision; newer changes are unpublished” when R18 exists. If the response is lost, the editor says publication is unconfirmed and checks the same operation key. It never asserts success from the elapsed eight seconds. Delete is separated, has no editor default mapping, and is unavailable with an explanation until publication is resolved.

## Acceptance checks and current status

**Passed — document inspection only:** All four original functions are retained in this contract; each has a label, role, scope and availability rule. The proposed state model covers pending, success, definite failure and uncertain completion. Local root, family routes, Buttons and Accessibility procedures and their guides were read. No implementation pass is implied.

**Failed — supplied design evidence:** Four prominent fills; destructive editor default; all 20 × 20 pt targets; unnamed Preview; absent upload feedback and duplicate suppression. These are specification failures, not executed device tests.

**Not executed — acceptance gates for implementation:**

1. Measure actual target regions: every action at least 44 × 44 pt, no overlap; verify proposed gaps and layout at narrow iPad editor widths and at least 200% text enlargement. Labels remain readable and all four functions reachable.
2. Inspect visual hierarchy in light/dark and increased contrast: only Publish has primary fill; Delete is recognizable without color. Measure actual contrast once colors/fonts exist.
3. Activate every command with supported touch, keyboard and assistive input. Confirm meaningful names, roles, focus, press feedback and busy states. Return in report text must not publish or delete. Closing Preview restores editor state; cancelling Delete changes nothing.
4. Inject an eight-second upload and bursts of activation through every input route: activity appears on initiation, one intent is submitted, and the server produces one publication. Verify unchanged button geometry and continued access to Preview/draft work.
5. Simulate definitive rejection, offline submission, lost acknowledgment after commit, repeated callbacks and navigation/reload. Preserve draft and operation identity; Retry cannot duplicate a committed report; stale callbacks cannot overwrite a newer operation.
6. Verify success only after acknowledged commit; newer edits stay unpublished. Test status announcement without focus theft or repeated chatter using VoiceOver and supported alternative input on an appropriate Apple environment.
7. Establish Delete'"'s real scope and undo guarantees. Test either complete restoration through Undo or explicit confirmation/cancellation, including all documented exits. Verify upload/Delete races cannot remove a report during unresolved publication.

## Evidence and routing limits

Only local files and installed instructions were used; no web request was made. Official links above identify the articles behind the local snapshot, not newly verified online guidance. The installed root is "'`.agents/skills/apple-hig/SKILL.md`; routes were read under `subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions`, `apple-hig-foundations`, `apple-hig-status`, and `apple-hig-presentation`. The Buttons and Accessibility `.topics/.../SKILL.md` procedures were successfully read before their `references/buttons.md` and `references/accessibility.md` guides.

The Status and Presentation routes link to `.topics/apple-hig-progress-indicators/SKILL.md` and `.topics/apple-hig-alerts/SKILL.md`, respectively, but reads found those files missing from this installed package. Their local `references/progress-indicators.md` and `references/alerts.md` guides were used as a limited fallback after the failed procedure reads. Full procedure compliance for those two topics cannot be claimed.

There is no rendered screen, source implementation, network service, deletion contract, SDK or runtime evidence. Contrast, actual focus order, native rendering, physical target comfort, accessibility execution and device behavior remain unverified. This deliverable corrects the written interaction contract; it does not implement or demonstrate it.

[Accessibility — Vision and Mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Mobility) supports meaningful descriptions and labeled controls. |
| 5 — Medium | Four equally prominent filled buttons conceal priority and give destructive Delete the same visual emphasis as routine actions. | Keep one filled primary, Publish. Use lower-emphasis Preview and Save Draft, and a spatially separate destructive Delete. Keep peer target heights consistent; use style rather than unequal sizes for hierarchy. [Buttons — Style](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons#Style) advises one or two prominent likely actions per view. |

The local guides differ in their numerical framing: Buttons gives general targets of at least 44 × 44 pt; Accessibility lists iPadOS 44 × 44 pt default and 28 × 28 pt minimum. This plan conservatively chooses 44 × 44 pt or larger. The supplied 20 × 20 pt fails both. The smaller accessibility minimum is not a reason to retain dense controls.

## Decisions and corrected action contract

All four are commands, so buttons remain appropriate; none represents persistent selection. The footer is retained. Proposed order: a separate leading Delete, then Save Draft, Preview, and trailing Publish. At narrow editor widths or enlarged text, wrap into stable rows with full labels and nonoverlapping targets; never shrink targets to fit. All custom buttons need visible press feedback, focus indication, and exposed enabled/busy states. Do not rely on red alone to identify Delete.

| Control | Outcome and scope | Role, availability and recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Publish | Publish a captured revision of the current report, including its attachments. This scope is a proposed contract, to validate against the service. | Sole primary, filled; enabled when publishable and no unresolved publish operation exists. It never deletes or dismisses unfinished work. Focused activation works; any editor-level default mapping must be Publish, never Delete, and must not intercept Return in text editing. |
| Preview | Open a read-only preview of the current report revision. | Normal, lower emphasis; visible and accessible label “Preview”. Closing returns to the editor and initiating control without losing edits. Remains usable during upload. |
| Save Draft | Persist the current editable report without publishing. | Normal, lower emphasis. Report actual save success/failure and preserve unsaved edits on failure. Remains usable during upload if draft persistence is independent; serialize it safely if the existing service shares mutable state. Never silently discard it. |
| Delete | Remove the current report, with exact local/remote scope disclosed before committing. | Destructive, lower emphasis, never the editor default. Block while Publish is unresolved, with nearby explanation “Available after publishing finishes.” |

Deletion recovery is not established by the brief. Conservative proposed behavior until its scope is resolved: activating Delete opens a confirmation identifying the report and exact loss, with Delete and Cancel and no default action. Cancel and supported keyboard cancellation leave the report intact and restore focus. Do not claim that confirmation already exists or is universally required. If investigation establishes routine, fully undoable deletion, prefer immediate deletion with a reliable Undo path instead of routine confirmation. If Assistive Access is supported, separately implement its documented two-confirmation treatment for difficult-to-reverse actions. [Alerts — Best practices and Buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts#Buttons) permits a default confirmation for deliberately requested destruction; the editor's unsafe default does not justify a blanket ban on that exception.

## Slow-upload state model

The eight seconds are observed duration in the brief, not a timer for declaring success. Show an indeterminate activity indicator **inside the activating Publish button**, replacing any image while retaining its label context and stable geometry. Use “Publishing…” and expose busy/unavailable semantics with a concise status announcement. Do not move focus or announce every animation frame. A spinner alone must not be the only accessible state.

Use measured progress only if the service can describe meaningful whole-operation completion; never invent percentages from elapsed time. If bytes reach 100% before server commit, say “Finishing publication…” rather than “Published”. Keep status in a stable location. Persistent success/error text should remain readable without a forced short timeout. [Progress indicators — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators#Best-practices) supports honest progress, stall explanation and safe cancellation.

"'```text
states = idle, publishing, reconciling, failed, published

activatePublish():                     // same handler for touch, keyboard, assistive input
  atomically:
    if state in {publishing, reconciling}: return
    if currentRevision already has acknowledged publication: show existing result; return
    capture immutable reportRevision and attachments
    obtain stable operationKey for this publication intent
    state = publishing                 // guard before starting asynchronous work
  render busy Publish("Publishing…"), status("Publishing report…")
  submit captured revision with operationKey

onAcknowledgedCommit(operationKey, publicationId):
  ignore callbacks for other operations
  record publicationId and captured revision durably
  state = published
  clear activity; show persistent "Published" and result link when available
  if editor has newer edits: show "Published revision; newer changes are unpublished"
  restore Publish only for a new publishable intent/revision

onDefinitiveFailure(operationKey):
  state = failed
  clear activity; show actionable reason and explicit Retry
  retain editor contents and captured operation context
  Retry reuses the key for the same intent

onTransportTimeoutOrLostResponse(operationKey):
  state = reconciling
  show "Publication not yet confirmed. Checking status…"
  query operation status; do not issue a new publication intent
  committed -> onAcknowledgedCommit
  definitively failed -> onDefinitiveFailure
  unknown -> retain guarded state with Check Status recovery
```

Server-side operation keys must return the same publication result for duplicate requests; a UI guard alone cannot cover retries or lost responses. Persist pending operation identity if navigation/reload can occur. These are proposed engineering requirements, not claims that the existing backend supports them. If no deduplication/status service exists, build that capability or expose an unresolved state that prevents unsafe retries; do not label uncertain publication as failed and start a fresh upload.

Keep editing, Preview and independent Save Draft usable; publish the captured revision rather than racing with later edits. Do not offer Cancel Upload until the service can guarantee what cancellation means. If safe cancellation is implemented, distinguish “request cancellation” from confirmed cancellation, preserve the draft, and resolve any concurrent server commit. No modal alert is needed for routine waiting.

## Worked before/after

**Before:** A field worker taps Publish at t=0. Nothing changes. At t=2 they tap again. The supplied behavior creates another upload. At approximately t=8 there is still no specified completion feedback. Delete remains equally prominent and the default.

**After (proposed):** At t=0 the first activation synchronously enters publishing and captures revision R17. Publish contains an activity indicator and reads “Publishing…”. At t=2 touch or keyboard reactivation creates no additional operation. Preview still opens R17/current content according to its clearly identified revision; later edits can be saved as R18. At t=8, **if** the server acknowledges R17, activity ends and the editor says “Published revision; newer changes are unpublished” when R18 exists. If the response is lost, the editor says publication is unconfirmed and checks the same operation key. It never asserts success from the elapsed eight seconds. Delete is separated, has no editor default mapping, and is unavailable with an explanation until publication is resolved.

## Acceptance checks and current status

**Passed — document inspection only:** All four original functions are retained in this contract; each has a label, role, scope and availability rule. The proposed state model covers pending, success, definite failure and uncertain completion. Local root, family routes, Buttons and Accessibility procedures and their guides were read. No implementation pass is implied.

**Failed — supplied design evidence:** Four prominent fills; destructive editor default; all 20 × 20 pt targets; unnamed Preview; absent upload feedback and duplicate suppression. These are specification failures, not executed device tests.

**Not executed — acceptance gates for implementation:**

1. Measure actual target regions: every action at least 44 × 44 pt, no overlap; verify proposed gaps and layout at narrow iPad editor widths and at least 200% text enlargement. Labels remain readable and all four functions reachable.
2. Inspect visual hierarchy in light/dark and increased contrast: only Publish has primary fill; Delete is recognizable without color. Measure actual contrast once colors/fonts exist.
3. Activate every command with supported touch, keyboard and assistive input. Confirm meaningful names, roles, focus, press feedback and busy states. Return in report text must not publish or delete. Closing Preview restores editor state; cancelling Delete changes nothing.
4. Inject an eight-second upload and bursts of activation through every input route: activity appears on initiation, one intent is submitted, and the server produces one publication. Verify unchanged button geometry and continued access to Preview/draft work.
5. Simulate definitive rejection, offline submission, lost acknowledgment after commit, repeated callbacks and navigation/reload. Preserve draft and operation identity; Retry cannot duplicate a committed report; stale callbacks cannot overwrite a newer operation.
6. Verify success only after acknowledged commit; newer edits stay unpublished. Test status announcement without focus theft or repeated chatter using VoiceOver and supported alternative input on an appropriate Apple environment.
7. Establish Delete'"'s real scope and undo guarantees. Test either complete restoration through Undo or explicit confirmation/cancellation, including all documented exits. Verify upload/Delete races cannot remove a report during unresolved publication.

Full procedure compliance for those two topics cannot be claimed.
